lines.text: Do you know how your phone takes bright photos in the dark?
You point it at the city at night. Hardly any light is reaching the sensor.
So the phone doesn't take one photo. It quietly grabs a whole burst of them, over a second or more.
Each one alone is dark and grainy. Random speckles of noise that change every single frame.
The phone lines the frames up, even if your hands shook a little.
Then it averages them. The real light adds up, and the random noise cancels out.
Finally it lifts the shadows and tames the bright lights. Night, turned almost into day.
Then send it with Orbi Transfer. The full photo, every pixel, to the friends right next to you.
